title: Female borrowers who include specific logistical details like working hours or commute distance may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who use broad, aspirational language regarding the future or community may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who express explicit thanks to lenders in their pitch may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who explicitly describe their business as thriving may fund faster.
Male borrowers who explicitly include their specific age in the pitch may fund faster.
Female borrowers who express explicit thanks to lenders may fund faster.
Female borrowers who write significantly lengthier pitches may fund faster.
Female borrowers who use more emotive language in their pitches may fund faster.
Female borrowers who emphasize personal history over business specifics may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who provide detailed descriptions of daily routines and childcare duties may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention benefits to their family or community fund faster.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that provide concrete financial figures or specific inventory lists fund faster regardless of gender.
Mentioning family obligations and benefits has opposite effects on funding speed by gender.
Mentioning local currency amounts or specific institutional affiliations predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who list the specific ages of their children fund faster.
Female borrowers who explicitly state their own age in the pitch fund more slowly.
